clips.title: 洛杉矶修人行横道：报价接近一百万美元，获批后还要等好几年？

subtitles.en: I read one of the things you're doing as part of your developing is you're building city infrastructure as well. So installing things like crosswalks. Yeah. What's the process of creating a crosswalk
subtitles.zh: 我了解到你们开发的一部分工作也包括建设城市基础设施，比如安装人行横道。那在洛杉矶，建一条人行横道的流程是怎样的？

subtitles.en: It's like a Kafka knob. It's just hollow. It's so small.
subtitles.zh: 这就像卡夫卡式的困境，空洞又琐碎。

subtitles.en: Oh, we got a great email. We got approved for a crosswalk on Clinton and Western. And it said it'll be built in a few years or more.
subtitles.zh: 我们收到一封邮件，说克林顿和西部大道的人行横道申请获批了，但还要等好几年才能建好。

subtitles.en: What's the constraint? What is the actual holdup? What's your sense of the holdup?
subtitles.zh: 瓶颈在哪里？到底是什么在拖延？你觉得拖延的原因是什么？

subtitles.en: There's no really process to get one. You have to pay for it. They're like, oh, yeah, we'll totally approve that for you. But it's going to cost the million dollars.
subtitles.zh: 其实没有真正的流程来申请。你得自己出钱。他们会说，哦，我们完全批准，但得花一百万美元。

subtitles.en: And then we're like, just to put a stop like a light and they're like, well, the engineering, the electrical. And then you got to go put a vault underneath for us.
subtitles.zh: 然后我们说，就装个红绿灯而已，他们却说，嗯，工程、电气，还得在下面给我们建个地下设施。

subtitles.en: So it's like, they're like, what are you going to do for us?
subtitles.zh: 所以就像，他们问，你打算为我们做什么？
en_highlights: what are you going to do

clip_research.source_claim: Installing a crosswalk in Los Angeles can cost around one million dollars and take years to approve and build, requiring engineering, electrical work, and an underground vault.
clip_research.public_baseline: Public summaries confirm that getting a crossing approved, engineered, and budgeted in LA can take years, and that a single crosswalk at Clinton and Western came with a price tag approaching one million dollars covering engineering, electrical work, and underground vault construction.
clip_research.surprise_gap: The transcript's claim that a simple crosswalk costs about $1 million and takes years is corroborated by public summaries, so the surprise is the scale of municipal infrastructure cost rather than a contradiction.

evidence.fact: Guest says a crosswalk at Clinton and Western was approved but will be built in a few years or more, and that the city quoted about one million dollars, citing engineering, electrical work, and an underground vault.

results.title: The Kafkaesque Reality of Building a Crosswalk in LA
results.snippet: Getting a crossing approved, engineered, and budgeted in Los Angeles can take years, if it happens at all; projects that survive that years-long process can still be rescinded on budget grounds. The asymmetry is the point: the city proved it could spend to erase a volunteer's $50 crosswalk faster than it could budget one of its own.

data_driven_lessons.source: KC桌面-视频号动态数据明细.csv, 114 rows, July 2026 local analysis
winning_patterns: 机构/人物权威 + 具体数字/资产 + 强问题，例如 高盛王逸：4-5万亿城市更新会拖住楼市吗
大机构/名人 + 被逼/陷阱/真相/转向 等张力词，例如 野村辜朝明：日本央行被逼到墙角
具体数据 + 政策动作疑问，例如 6月PMI释放积极信号，政府会加码吗
反常识判断 + 下一步条件，例如 低估值可能是价值陷阱，需等待政策转向消费
中国相关议题更容易获得点击，但表达要落在政策、需求、信心、估值、产业升级这些正向框架
外资或海外权威给出对中国更积极的判断时，反差本身就是主标题，不要埋在摘要里
让观众产生单一强反应：居然如此、终于有人说、他说的是真的吗、原来中国优势在这里
大实话角度来自表达者身份与观点反差；言行反差角度必须有公开动作或披露支撑
涉及中国比较优势时，优先把外国企业被迫调整、海外权威改口或中国优势被低估写成冲突
avoid_patterns: 过长的新闻句，尤其是 24 字以上还塞多个从句
只有 策略/机会/影响/前瞻/市场/风险 这类泛词，没有具体对象或张力
美国宏观泛标题如果没有美联储/鲍威尔等强锚点，点击明显弱
纯描述式标题，例如 某市场短期风险与长期催化剂，缺少问题和冲突
经济危机/金融危机/崩盘/崩溃 这类过硬负面财经词
把事实换成疑问号但没有反差，例如 回报路径在哪、未来如何、能否实现
陌生英文人名或机构全称占据第一行，却没有告诉观众这个人为什么值得听
把 Bloomberg LP 等来源或公司法律后缀误当成采访对象
没有公开证据却暗示嘉宾撒谎、操纵或言行不一
